doom.driver: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit.
doom.blurb: TWO SUPERPOWERS, ONE ALGORITHM, NO PLAN
doom.summary: The US and China are meeting to discuss AI safety guardrails — which sounds reassuring until you realize the summit is also the backdrop for Ukraine drone-striking Moscow, the UN declaring US drug boat attacks potential crimes against humanity, and Trump floating an 'AI Force' while his treasury secretary refuses to give AI companies a liability shield. The adults are in the room; unfortunately so is everyone else.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Trump's 'AI Force' proposal and a US-China AI hotline discussion signal that AI is now firmly a geopolitical weapons category, not just a tech category.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: The UN's first major AI assessment warns governments must rein in AI agents before risks are understood — while the US refuses liability shields for AI companies.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Ukraine launched 1,000+ drones at Moscow on Russia's election day, a Houthi missile targeted Riyadh, and the Saudi East-West pipeline is shut down — multiple pressure points flaring simultaneously.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Jensen Huang publicly dismissing AI safety fears while researchers warn otherwise is exactly the kind of narrative gap that precedes surprises.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: The UN GA convening amid wars in Ukraine and the Gulf, a Trump-Xi summit, and US press bans being litigated in real time makes for a combustible diplomatic week.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — silhouette composition, deep navy and smoldering orange palette, heavy shadows dominate, warmth feels threatening — we are inside a darkened Manhattan high-rise office at night, looking outward through floor-to-ceiling glass windows toward the glowing amber smear of the midtown skyline beyond, the Hudson River a black ribbon far below catching orange reflections — in the foreground, two human silhouettes stand close together but not touching, one slightly taller, both in formal suit jackets, their backs to us, facing the window and the city glow, their outlines crisp and featureless against the burning cityscape behind them — between them on a long dark conference table: a single smartphone screen glowing cold blue-white upward like a lantern, the only cool light in the frame, casting faint underlit shadows on their chins — on the table's surface, two small flag stands are silhouetted, their miniature banners indistinct but present — the ceiling is low and dark, fluorescent panels dead or dimmed, only the city outside providing illumination — the orange glow from the skyline halos the two figures like heat from something enormous and unseen, the mood ceremonial but suffocating, the silence between the two figures heavier than any spoken word.

dawn.driver: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit. Top US and Chinese officials held talks in New York on Sunday ahead of a Trump-Xi summit this week.
dawn.blurb: THE TWO SUPERPOWERS ARE ACTUALLY TALKING ABOUT AI SAFETY
dawn.summary: In a week dominated by rogue AI incidents and war crime allegations, the world's two most powerful nations quietly sat down to discuss guardrails for artificial intelligence before it outpaces both of them. The US-China AI safety talks — including discussion of a mutual incident notification 'hotline' — represent exactly the kind of great-power cooperation that most analysts assumed was dead. It won't fix everything, but two rivals choosing dialogue over competition on the defining technology of our era is a signal worth holding onto.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: US and Chinese officials holding substantive AI safety talks ahead of a Trump-Xi summit is the kind of diplomatic back-channel that prevents catastrophic misunderstanding between nuclear-armed rivals.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: NASA successfully powered up Roman Space Telescope's massive 300-megapixel infrared camera, a milestone for a mission that will survey more of the cosmos than any instrument before it.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: A UT freshman won $1.1 million at ESPN's College GameDay kicking contest, a perfectly ridiculous reminder that ordinary people get extraordinary moments.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: A new Amazon study identifies the most effective strategies for protecting biodiversity and carbon, giving conservationists a clearer roadmap for where intervention matters most.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Egypt's Amina Orfi became the youngest women's squash world number one at just 19, a landmark for African sport and a reminder that talent has no geography.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Night scene, all light from artificial sources, deep shadows dominating. The environment is a cramped late-night convenience store or bodega interior, shelves of goods receding into darkness behind a single glowing television mounted high on the wall, its blue-white screen light the only warm source in the room, casting long amber and teal shadows across stacked cans and a cluttered counter below. The TV screen displays two silhouetted figures seated across a table from one another, a faint circuit-line glow between them suggesting a shared screen or document, the New York skyline ghosted in the background of the broadcast. A solitary figure — a store clerk — leans forward on the counter, elbows down, chin resting in one hand, watching the broadcast with quiet, tired attention. Two small paper flags, American and Chinese, are pinned to the corkboard beside the register, barely visible in the peripheral darkness. The floor reflects the television's cold blue light in long liquid streaks across worn linoleum. Deep shadows consume the corners. Mood is still, watchful, the world absorbing something quietly significant at the edge of midnight. Deep golden hour amber and warm teal palette filtered through the artificial blue of the screen glow. Radiant screen light, long shadows, 16-bit SNES pixel art, no text, no antialiasing.
